existing_sources_reused.title: E. P. Thompson, “Time, Work-Discipline, and Industrial Capitalism,” Past & Present 38 (1967): 56–97.
existing_sources_reused.citation: E. P. Thompson, “Time, Work-Discipline, and Industrial Capitalism,” Past & Present 38 (1967): 56–97.

verification.note: Downloaded primary scan: opening pp. 56–62 and selected concluding passages pp. 89–97 read; some extracted passages/notes were truncated, so no full-article reading claimed. Explicit resources include Le Goff, Febvre, Evans-Pritchard and Bourdieu. Employment relations complicate task/clock distinctions; education, religion and coercion matter alongside clocks. Concluding criticism of Moore/Kerr/Siegel contests treating workers as inert inputs. Thompson’s own developmental assumptions and cultural comparisons remain situated arguments, not a proven universal sequence.
